ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, some glass cups of the same shape can be seen stacked up and down into a regular pile of cups. On the left is a taller stack of cups, and on the right is a shorter stack of cups; the cups are identical and nested, so each additional cup will only add the same segment of visible height. Reasoning: Model the total height of n cups as H(n)=a+(n-1)d, where a represents the base height formed by the bottom cup itself, and d represents the height added by each additional nested cup. The problem gives that 8 cups are 42 cm high, so a+7d=42; 2 cups are 18 cm high, so a+d=18. Subtracting the two equations gives 6d=24, therefore d=4. From a+d=18, a=14. The height of six cups is H(6)=a+5d=14+5×4=34 cm.

method.method_draft: Model the stack height as a fixed bottom-glass height plus a constant extra height for each additional identical nested glass. Read from the image that the glasses are identical and nested in a regular stack, so each added glass contributes the same visible increment. Read from the text that 8 glasses measure 42 cm and 2 glasses measure 18 cm. Set H(n)=a+(n-1)d. Then a+7d=42 and a+d=18, so 6d=24 and d=4; hence a=14. For 6 glasses, H(6)=14+5·4=34 cm.
